original_question: Find the asymptotic value of subset(L_d) when L_d is the d-dimensional integer lattice n^(1/d) x ... x n^(1/d), where subset(L_d) is the size of the largest subset whose positive distances are all unique.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 24 (Erdős and Guy): the higher-dimensional lattice special case of the paper's "subsets with no repeated distances" problem. In the June 7, 2014 PDF draft hosted by the author, the same target appears as Section 5, Problem 23.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the intended special-case open problem: determine the asymptotic behavior of subset(L_d) for a d-dimensional integer lattice L_d, where one seeks the largest subset whose nonzero pairwise distances are all different.
missing_details: The metric should be stated explicitly: these are Euclidean distances in R^d.
The uniqueness condition is over all unordered pairs of distinct points in the subset: no two different pairs may determine the same positive distance.

The nearby definition makes clear that repeated distances count even when the two equal-length pairs share a point; the condition is stronger than merely forbidding two disjoint pairs of the same length.
L_d should be specified as a d-dimensional section of the integer lattice Z^d of side length n^(1/d), i.e. an n-point grid up to the usual perfect-dth-power convention.
The asymptotic regime should be made explicit: n tends to infinity with d fixed.
In the paper this is the lattice-specialized problem subset(L_d), not the more general extremal function subset_d(n) for arbitrary n-point sets in R^d.
For a fully stand-alone statement, subset(L_d) should be defined as an explicit maximum over subsets S ⊂ L_d.
refined_question: Fix an integer d >= 3, and assume n is a perfect dth power. Let L_d = {1,2,...,n^(1/d)}^d ⊂ Z^d ⊂ R^d. Define subset(L_d) to be the maximum cardinality of a subset S ⊂ L_d such that no two distinct unordered pairs of points of S determine the same positive Euclidean distance; equivalently, every nonzero distance spanned by S occurs at most once. Find the asymptotic value of subset(L_d) as n -> infinity.
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the lattice-specialized open problem from the section on subsets with no repeated distances, not the general function subset_d(n). The paper first defines subset(P) as the largest subset of a point set P in which no positive distance is repeated, then asks for the asymptotic value of subset(L_d) when L_d is a d-dimensional integer lattice of side length n^(1/d). The immediately surrounding context records the known bounds subset(L_d) = Ω(n^(2/(3d))) and subset(L_d) = O(n^(1/d)); the upper bound comes from the earlier higher-dimensional observation that such a lattice determines only O(n^(2/d)) distinct distances. To make the question stand alone while staying faithful to the paper, one must specify the Euclidean ambient space, the exact pairwise nonrepetition condition, the lattice as a section of Z^d, and the asymptotic regime n -> infinity for fixed d. The planar case d = 2 is treated separately just before this higher-dimensional lattice problem.
